title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #1
body: Sit outside Headstart Kuri or Froebel's at two o'clock and you've read the city. If a Prado pulls up and nobody gets out of the driver's seat, that's a driver. If a seventeen-year-old drives off in a Civic with no licence and zero concern, that's a family that has never had a problem a phone call couldn't fix. It's a sealed deal if the guard lifts the barrier before the car even slows down.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #2
body: Ask where they were last night and listen for the market. "Kohsar," "Jinnah Super," "Rana Market," and they'll assume you know which corner. Chaaye Khana at eleven. Street 1 for brunch. Burning Brownie when someone's upset. It's a sealed deal if they've ordered the same thing at the same place since O Levels and the man there starts making it on sight.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #3
body: Ask what happens after school and listen for the word tutor. Not academy, tutor, who comes to the house, one subject, forty thousand a month. The academy kids are a different tier and both sides know it. It's a sealed deal if that tutor taught the older sibling first and has been coming to that house for nine years.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #4
body: Summer sorts them. "We're going up to Murree" is one lobby. "We're doing Hunza" is the photograph. "We go to London every year, my cousins are there" is the one you're looking for, and it is never called a holiday. It's a sealed deal if there's a flat somewhere they have never once referred to as a hotel.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #5
body: Islamabad has no nightlife so the drive is the nightlife. Margalla Road with the windows down, chai at a dhaba on Ninth Avenue, then the Faisal Mosque loop at one in the morning. Nobody is going anywhere. That's the whole point. It's a sealed deal if they have a specific forty-minute loop they drive alone when they're thinking.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #6
body: Compare his car to the car at home. The son has the loud one, a Civic with an exhaust or a wrapped Vezel. The father drives a white Prado with a dent he has never fixed in four years. It costs three times as much. It's a sealed deal if he laughs when you ask about his dad's car, because that laugh is the entire class system.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #7
body: Watch what happens when the light goes, because it doesn't. The generator catches in two seconds and nobody pauses mid-sentence. There's a bore, so a tanker has never been discussed in that house. That is the real privilege and it's completely invisible from inside. It's a sealed deal if a teenager there cannot tell you what load-shedding actually means.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Islamabad. Tip #8
body: Ask about university and the plan is already closed. "NUST, hopefully" is the version for relatives. Abroad was decided when the kid was fourteen. If they're doing A Levels instead of FSc they were never staying, and everyone at that table worked it out years ago. It's a sealed deal if a UCAS deadline caused more stress in that house than any exam ever did.
